sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Sittard is rewriting a parking policy that dates from 2009 and 2012. The outline note of the Parkeerbeleidsplan 2025-2040, published in the municipal gazette on 10 March 2026, says the current policy no longer fits. It works in two phases: first alternatives and, for the centre, more subscriptions and differentiated tariffs, and later more steering, such as fewer permits and progressive tariffs; these are plans and not yet rules [0]. For the centre the note says it stays well reachable by car, with no extra capacity in the inner city apart from new developments, while street parking is to be scaled back in phase 2 where public space needs a different use; the core shopping area stays car-light [1]. Paid parking runs Monday to Saturday from 09.00 to 19.00, with late shopping evenings until 22.00 and Sundays from 12.00 to 18.00, at 1.90 euros an hour as the normal rate [2]. In February 2025 the college said free parking on shopping Sundays, from 26 May to December 2024, cost about 130,000 euros in lost revenue and was not continued in 2025, and it declined a free-weekday pilot and copying Geleen's two free hours [8]. In January 2026 it again declined a general free or lower rate, having decided on 8 July 2025 to make parking free on every Sunday in December and given traders about 2,000 cards worth 2 euros off in Odaparking; it would study temporary incentives during the works [9]. A version of the permit rules valid from 23 December 2025 to 6 February 2026 capped one centre permit per address, with up to 3 plates, at locations such as 140 for Walramstraat, Heinseweg and Overhovenerstraat; the current rules were not found [10].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The city centre is under construction. A resident letter of 4 March 2026 said BESIX Infra Nederland would rebuild Wilhelminastraat, Engelenkampstraat and Tempelplein in phases until the end of 2027, starting on 7 April 2026 [12]. On the Tempelplein the college decided to keep 51 parking spaces, eight of them for disabled people, although the earlier masterplan foresaw none, and a council motion calls for at least 35 to stay reachable during the works [11]. Around the station, the Sittard Centraal programme plans a 2045 vision of up to 4,689 new homes, and the outline note proposes low parking norms there and more bicycle parking [16]. Vattenfall is responsible for new public charge points in 2024 to 2028, with a placement policy adopted on 25 March 2025; the municipal page did not report the outcome of the round announced for 2026 [14]. Car ownership rose from 1.14 per household in 2015 to 1.21 in 2024, and the Sittard core has the lowest figure at 1.02 [15].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality owns and runs almost all its public garages itself, which a December 2023 report called unusual for a Dutch town; for 2022 it put parking income at about 6.3 million euros against costs of about 5.8 million [6]. For 2025 the garages cost 1.90 euros an hour at Hub Dassenplein and the ABC deck, up to 10 euros a day, and at Odaparking up to 5 euros a day; Geleen's Marktgarage is 1 euro an hour with two hours free, and we found no 2026 decision [3]. A resident subscription costs 120 euros a year, an office-hours subscription 522 euros and a 24/7 subscription 1,065 euros [4]. In February 2025 the college admitted defects at Odaparking, with water ingress, broken lifts and charge points switched off, and said two of three lifts were being replaced [13]. A parking count of November 2024 found Saturday 14:00 peaks of 48 percent at Hub Dassenplein, 47 percent at Odaparking and 74 percent at the ABC deck, and none of the garages ever full except Geleen's Marktgarage, while pressure was higher around the centre, which the note puts down to possibly missing regulation [5]. Q-Park runs the P+R Transferium at the station, with 525 spaces and 12 charge points; its tariff table failed to load [7].

Our data cover that park-and-ride, whose feed gives 500 spaces, for 48 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 27% on weekdays and 16% at weekends, with a peak of 77% around midday on a Tuesday. The capacity differs slightly from Q-Park's figure, so the percentages are approximate. The garages in the centre are not in our data.
